answer: The violet counter is kept in wander and kernel makes public each reset. A bond is refunded only after 50 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. A hostile operator therefore has to keep every alias continuously active for 50 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. That bill is paid per identity, so 155 aliases cost 400 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
